2607.16097.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
2607.16097.paper_summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become central to improving large language models (LLMs) on complex reasoning tasks, yet RL post-training is largely studied in isolation from the pretraining that precedes it. As a result, two basic questions remain open: (1) how do pretraining choices (model size, data) shape the returns to RL compute, and (2) what does RL actually do to the model? These questions are difficult to study in the standard LLM setting: pretraining corpora are vast and uncontrolled, making it hard to attribute behaviors to pretraining versus RL, and systematic compute sweeps across both stages are prohibitively expensive. To address these challenges, we use chess as a controlled testbed for studying reasoning across the full pretraining-to-post-training pipeline. We follow the standard LLM training pipeline by pretraining language models from 5M to 1B parameters on human chess games, supervised fine-tuning on synthetic reasoning traces, and running RL on chess puzzles with verifiable rewards. Using this framework, we find that the post-RL performance at given RL compute level is well-predicted from the pretraining loss, and slope of the RL reward curves improves approximately linearly with the pretraining tokens. Beyond scaling, we find that RL does not simply sharpen the SFT policy: on easy puzzles it amplifies correct moves the SFT policy already preferred, while on hard puzzles it surfaces correct moves that were nearly absent under SFT. We further test whether our findings transfer beyond chess by training a 1B language model on math-domain text, where the same predictive pattern emerges: longer-pretrained checkpoints reach higher post-RL performance and improve faster under RL. In sum, we provide a quantitative account of the pretraining-to-RL interface and a controlled testbed for studying the science of reasoning across the full pretraining-to-post-training pipeline.
2607.16097.paper_summary_zh: 強化學習（RL）已成為提高大型語言模型（LLMs）在複雜推理任務中的核心，但RL後訓練在很大程度上是與其前的預訓練隔離研究的。因此，兩個基本問題仍然懸而未決：（1）預訓練的選擇（模型大小、數據）如何影響RL計算的回報，以及（2）RL實際上對模型做了什麼？在標準LLM設置中，這些問題難以研究：預訓練語料庫龐大且不受控制，使得很難將行為歸因於預訓練與RL之間，並且在兩個階段之間進行系統性計算掃描的成本過高。為了解決這些挑戰，我們使用棋類作為控制測試平台來研究整個預訓練到後訓練管道中的推理。我們遵循標準的LLM訓練管道，從5M到1B參數的語言模型在人體棋局上進行預訓練，對合成推理痕跡進行監督微調，並在具有可驗證獎勵的棋類謎題上運行RL。利用這一框架，我們發現給定RL計算水平的後RL性能可以很好地從預訓練損失中預測，並且RL獎勵曲線的斜率隨著預訓練標記的增加而大約線性改善。除了擴展外，我們發現RL並不僅僅是加強SFT策略：在簡單的謎題中，它放大了SFT策略已經偏好的正確移動，而在困難的謎題中，它顯示出在SFT下幾乎不存在的正確移動。我們進一步測試我們的發現是否能超越棋類，通過在數學領域文本上訓練1B語言模型，發現相同的預測模式出現：預訓練時間更長的檢查點達到更高的後RL性能，並在RL下改善得更快。總之，我們提供了對預訓練到RL界面的定量說明，以及一個控制測試平台，用於研究整個預訓練到後訓練管道中的推理科學。
